name: Eswatini
summary: Blue, yellow, crimson, yellow and blue horizontal stripes with a black and white Nguni shield, two spears and a staff with tassels in the centre. It is based on a military banner given by King Sobhuza II in 1941.
origin: King Sobhuza II gave a banner to the Swazi Pioneer Corps that served in the Second World War; it formed the basis of the national flag, adopted on 6 October 1968, a month after independence.

symbols.name: Nguni shield
symbols.description: A black and white oxhide shield laid horizontally.
symbols.meaning: Protection of the country; the black and white show that Black and white people live in peace together.

symbols.name: Spears and staff
symbols.description: Two assegais and a staff decorated with tassels of widow bird feathers (injobo).
symbols.meaning: Protection; the feathers are a sign of royalty.

facts: The country changed its English name from Swaziland to Eswatini in 2018.
Eswatini is one of the world's last absolute monarchies.
Kenya's flag also shows a shield and two spears.
